newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES FIRMER AS LIQUIDITY EASES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES FIRMER AS LIQUIDITY EASES.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged up on Monday in reflection of a lower level of liquidity in the system, dealers said.
"The market is a little bit dry -- we're not expecting any maturities at all today-- and rates have come up a bit," one dealer commented."
He said discount houses were taking up 91-day central bank paper at a steady 21.46 percent but were selling them firmer on the market at 21.35 percent from Friday's 21.25.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold half a percent point harder at 23.50 and 22.50 percent respectively while bankers acceptances were quoted at 22 and 21.5 percent from 21.75 and 21.25 percent across the board.
Call money added one-and-a-half percent to 23 percent in a market which opened in surplus of Z$38 million, down from Z$382 million on Friday.
